rationale: This record is a theoretical/historical article on clinical social work practitioner discretion in direct practice and health care settings. It has no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access (fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4, E01) and presents practice theory commentary rather than empirical primary research or a systematic review on water/sanitation access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both readings due to E01 (non-water/sanitation topic: clinical social work practice in health care). Although practitioner discretion and accountability measures touch general administrative concepts under the broad plain reading of Criterion 2, the record fails Criterion 1, Criterion 3, and Criterion 4 under both readings.

evidence_quotes.quote: Discretion in Direct Practice: New Perspectives
Because the mediational model of discretionbased social work intervention originated in health care, a field that today employs the largest concentration of social workers in this country
the ethical aspects of practitioner decision making assumed dominant importance in practice theory (Reamer, 2001).
